questions.question: Let [latex]S[/latex] be the set of all ternary strings defined over the alphabet [latex]\{a, b, c\}[/latex]. Consider all strings in [latex]S[/latex] that contain at least one occurrence of two consecutive symbols, that is, "aa", "bb" or "cc". The number of such strings of length 5 that are possible is _______. (Answer in integer)
questions.explanation:
Total ternary strings of length [latex]5[/latex] over [latex]\{a,b,c\}[/latex]: [latex]3^5=243[/latex].

It's easier to count the complement: strings with no two consecutive equal symbols anywhere. The first symbol has [latex]3[/latex] choices; each subsequent symbol just needs to differ from its immediate predecessor, giving [latex]2[/latex] choices each time: [latex]3\times2^4=3\times16=48[/latex] such "no-repeat" strings.

So strings containing at least one consecutive repeat [latex]=243-48=195[/latex].

Answer: 195

questions.question: Let G be a finite group on 84 elements. The size of a largest possible proper subgroup of G is ________.
questions.explanation:
By Lagrange's theorem the order of a subgroup divides 84. The largest proper divisor of 84 is 42 (index 2).

Answer: 42

questions.question: Suppose U is the power set of the set S={1,2,3,4,5,6}. For any T[latex]\in[/latex]U, let |T| denote the number of elements in T and T' denote the complement of T. For any T,R[latex]\in[/latex]U, let T\R be the set of all elements in T which are not in R. Which one of the following is true?

options.B: [latex]\exists X\in U \; \exists Y\in U \; [/latex] [latex](|X|=5,\; |Y|=5 \; and \;  X \cap  Y=\phi )[/latex]
options.C: [latex]\forall X\in U \; \forall Y\in U \;[/latex] [latex] (|X|=2,\; |Y|=3 \; and \; X \setminus  Y=\phi )[/latex]
options.D: [latex]\forall X \in U \; \forall Y\in U\; (X \setminus  Y=Y' \setminus  X')[/latex]

questions.explanation:
[latex]X\setminus Y=X\cap Y'[/latex] and [latex]Y'\setminus X'=Y'\cap X[/latex]. These are the same set for every X, Y.

- Option 1 fails for X = {1}.
- Option 2: two 5-element subsets of a 6-element set must overlap.
- Option 3 is not true for all X, Y.

Answer: [latex]\forall X\,\forall Y\,(X\setminus Y=Y'\setminus X')[/latex]

questions.question:
For a set A, the power set of A is denoted by [latex]2^{A}[/latex]. If A={5,{6},{7}}, which of the following options are TRUE?
I. [latex]\phi \in 2^{A}[/latex]
II. [latex]\phi \subseteq 2^{A}[/latex]
III. {5,{6}} [latex]\in 2^{A}[/latex]
IV. {5,{6}}[latex]\subseteq 2^{A}[/latex]
questions.explanation:
Checking each statement:
- I: [latex]\phi\subseteq A[/latex], so [latex]\phi\in2^A[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- II: the empty set is a subset of every set [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- III: {5, {6}} [latex]\subseteq[/latex] A, so it is an element of [latex]2^A[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] True
- IV: would need 5 [latex]\in2^A[/latex], but 5 is not a subset of A [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] False

Answer: I, II and III only

questions.question:
The security system at an IT office is composed of 10 computers of which exactly four are
working. To check whether the system is functional, the officials inspect four of the
computers picked at random (without replacement). The system is deemed functional if at
least three of the four computers inspected are working. Let the probability that the system is deemed functional be denoted by p.  Then 100p= _____________.
questions.explanation:
4 working, 6 not working. Choose 4 computers: [latex]\binom{10}{4}=210[/latex] ways.

- Exactly 3 working: [latex]\binom43\binom61=24[/latex]
- All 4 working: [latex]\binom44=1[/latex]

[latex]p=\frac{25}{210}=0.119\Rightarrow 100p\approx 11.9[/latex]

Answer: 11.9

questions.question: Let [latex]\delta[/latex] denote the minimum degree of a vertex in a graph. For all planar graphs on n vertices with [latex]\delta \geq 3[/latex], which one of the following is TRUE?

options.A: In any planar embedding, the number of faces is at least [latex]\frac{n}{2}+2[/latex]
options.B: In any planar embedding, the number of faces is less than [latex]\frac{n}{2}+2[/latex]
options.C: There is a planar embedding in which the number of faces is less than [latex]\frac{n}{2}+2[/latex]
options.D: There is a planar embedding in which the number of faces is at most [latex]\frac{n}{\delta +1}[/latex]

questions.explanation:
[latex]\delta\ge3\Rightarrow 2e=\sum\deg\ge3n\Rightarrow e\ge\frac{3n}{2}[/latex]

Euler: [latex]f=e-n+2\ge\frac{3n}{2}-n+2=\frac n2+2[/latex], for every planar embedding.

Answer: In any planar embedding, the number of faces is at least [latex]\frac n2+2[/latex]

[latex]=\left(1+2+5+7\right)\times\dfrac{1}{6}+\left(3+4+6+8\right)\times\dfrac{1}{12}[/latex]

questions.question:
Let p, q, and r be propositions and the expression (p[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]q)[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]r be a contradiction. Then, the
expression (r[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]p)[latex]\rightarrow[/latex]q is

options.C: always TRUE when p is FALSE
options.D: always TRUE when q is TRUE

questions.explanation:
[latex](p\rightarrow q)\rightarrow r[/latex] is always false, so [latex]p\rightarrow q[/latex] is always true and r is always false.

Then [latex]r\rightarrow p[/latex] is true (r is false), so [latex](r\rightarrow p)\rightarrow q\equiv q[/latex]. It is true exactly when q is true.

Answer: always TRUE when q is TRUE

questions.question:
Which one of the following propositional logic formulas is TRUE when exactly two of p, q,
and r are TRUE?
questions.explanation:
Exactly two true means either r is true with exactly one of p, q (that is [latex]\neg(p\leftrightarrow q)\wedge r[/latex]), or p and q true with r false ([latex]p\wedge q\wedge\sim r[/latex]). Option 2 is exactly the OR of these two cases.

Answer: Option 2
